transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thanks. Um, so I'm a high school teacher, and I came in because... well, I just can't seem to get through my work. Like, I can sit down at my desk with a whole stack of essays or a new curriculum document, totally ready and fully intending to work. 

Which, by the way, the new curriculum documents this year are just ridiculously long. The school district completely overhauled the standards over the summer, and they didn't even give us the new rubrics until like, three weeks into the term. It’s been a total mess. My co-teacher was actually saying he might just retire early because of how disorganized the administration is, and I honestly don't blame him, we had this whole meeting about it on Tuesday and... 

Anyway, sorry. The point is, I'll sit down to grade those essays or read the new standards, and within ten minutes I'll realize I’ve just been staring at the exact same page. I'll be sitting there thinking about three completely different things, and I'm barely taking in a single word of what’s right in front of me. So, yeah, that's why I made the appointment.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time lately?

Sad? No, I wouldn't say I've been feeling sad. I mean, I get frustrated sometimes, sure, but not like... depressed or down most of the time. Actually, speaking of feeling down, my sister just got a new puppy—a golden retriever mix—and it is literally impossible to be sad around that dog. I went over to her place this weekend, and he just kept bringing me this half-chewed tennis ball, dropping it right on my foot, and then staring at me with those huge eyes. She named him Barnaby, which I think is kind of a weird name for a dog, but it suits him perfectly. He’s got these giant floppy ears that drag on the floor when he sniffs around. Anyway, she was telling me about the puppy training classes they're taking, and the trainer apparently uses this whole clicker method... wait, what was the question again? Oh, right, feeling sad. Yeah, no, I don't think I've been feeling sad. Just frustrated with work, really.
Have you been feeling anxious lately?

Anxious? Um, no, not really. I mean, I guess I get a little stressed when I look at the pile of grading I have to do, but I don't think it's anxiety. It's more just... annoyance, you know? Like, I have this one student, Michael, and he's a great kid, really smart, but his handwriting is absolutely atrocious. It looks like a spider fell in an inkwell and just walked all over the page. I actually tried to get him to type his assignments, and I even brought it up at the parent-teacher conference last month. His mom was super defensive about it, though. She was wearing this huge, bright yellow scarf, which was kind of distracting, honestly. But she insisted that his previous teachers never had an issue with it, which I find really hard to believe because I literally have to hold his papers up to the light sometimes just to make out a single letter. And then there's the whole issue of the school's new policy on late work, which is a whole other headache... but yeah, no, not anxious. Just, you know, regular teacher stress.
How long can you usually focus on a single task outside of work, like reading a book or watching a movie?

Um, outside of work? Well, I don't really know, honestly. I mean, I try to read sometimes. I picked up this sci-fi novel a couple weeks ago because my buddy Dan recommended it. Dan and I actually used to play in a band together back in college, if you can believe that. He played bass, and I was on drums. We were terrible, like, really objectively bad, but we played this one gig at a local dive bar—The Rusty Anchor, I think it was called—and the sound system was so busted that nobody could even tell we were messing up half the songs. They had these sticky floors and a jukebox that only played 80s hair metal. Dan actually spilled a whole pitcher of beer on his amp that night... it was a disaster. But anyway, what were we talking about? Oh, right, focusing on stuff. Yeah, I don't really know how long I can focus on things like that. I just sort of... don't keep track, I guess.
Do you often find yourself fidgeting or feeling restless when you're sitting still?

Fidgeting? Um, I don't know, not really? I mean, I don't feel like I have to be running around or anything. I do tap my foot a lot, I guess. Actually, speaking of tapping, I bought this really nice mechanical keyboard for my home office a few months ago. It has those Cherry MX Blue switches, you know? The ones that make that incredibly satisfying click-clack sound when you type. I thought it would make grading papers more fun, but it turns out my microphone picks up every single keystroke when I'm on a video call. I had a parent-teacher zoom meeting last week with Michael's mom—the one with the yellow scarf—and she actually stopped mid-sentence to ask if I was eating chips because of the crunching sound. I had to explain it was just my keyboard. I ended up having to buy a desk mat to try and dampen the sound, which led me down this massive rabbit hole of custom desk setups on YouTube. There's this whole community of people who build their own keyboards from scratch, soldering the switches and everything. It's wild how much money people spend on... wait, sorry, what did you ask me? Restless? Yeah, no, I don't think I'm really restless. I can sit in a chair fine.
Do you often interrupt others when they're talking?

Interrupt? Um, no, I don't think so. I'm usually pretty quiet when other people are talking. Like in our staff meetings, I basically never say anything. Our principal, Mr. Henderson, he can talk for like forty-five minutes straight without taking a breath. It's actually kind of impressive. He always wears these incredibly loud novelty ties, too. Last week he had one with little cartoon golf clubs all over it. Which is funny because I'm pretty sure he doesn't even golf. 

My brother-in-law golfs, though. He actually just had his wedding at this fancy country club out in the suburbs, and the catering was unbelievable. They had this mashed potato bar where they served the potatoes in martini glasses. You could put bacon and chives and all this stuff on top. I must have eaten like three glasses of potatoes. I couldn't even dance afterwards because I was so full. The DJ was terrible anyway, he kept playing all these weird techno remixes of 90s R&B songs... 

Wait, sorry, what were you asking? Oh, interrupting. Right. No, I don't really interrupt people. I usually just let them finish.
Can you tell me about the last time you tried to complete a hobby or project in your free time, and how that went?

Um, a hobby or project? Well... I'm not really sure. I mean, I start a lot of things. Like, a couple of months ago, I decided I was going to get really into making sourdough bread. Everyone was doing it, and it seemed like a cool science experiment, you know? So I bought the flour, got this glass jar for the starter, and gave it a name—Doughy Ramone. I even bought this special scoring lame to make those pretty patterns on the top of the bread. 

Actually, the lame had this beautiful wooden handle, which made me think about maybe getting into woodworking. My grandfather used to do woodworking. He had this huge shop in his garage filled with all these vintage tools. He made me this wooden rocking horse when I was a kid, and it was so sturdy that my cousin's kids are still using it today. My cousin lives out in Colorado now, near the mountains. She sends these amazing pictures of the snow. I've always wanted to go skiing, but honestly, the idea of getting on a chairlift terrifies me. I saw this video once of a chairlift swinging backward in a windstorm, and it just looked like an absolute nightmare... 

Wait, what was the question? Oh, right, completing a project. Yeah, I don't know. I guess I don't really finish a lot of them. The sourdough starter just kind of died in the fridge because I forgot to feed it. So... yeah, I don't really have a good example of finishing one.
Do you often blur out answers before the person finishes asking the question?

Blurting out answers? Um, no, not really. I usually wait until someone is done talking. I think I'm pretty good at waiting my turn in conversations. It's kind of like in my classroom, right? I try to teach the kids to raise their hands and not just yell out the answers. Though, to be fair, seventh graders are basically incapable of holding a thought for more than two seconds without shouting it. 

I actually have this one kid, Tyler, who sits in the front row. Great kid, super smart, but he just cannot stay in his seat. Yesterday, he brought in this massive collection of Pokémon cards to show his friends before the bell rang. I haven't seen Pokémon cards since I was like, ten. I had this holographic Charizard that I traded for a bunch of terrible cards because I didn't know what it was worth. My mom was so mad when she found out. She used to keep all my valuable cards in this old cigar box on top of the fridge so I wouldn't ruin them. 

The fridge in our staff room is actually broken right now, which is a total disaster. Someone left a tuna sandwich in there over the weekend, and the smell is just... it's haunting the entire second floor. The janitor, Mr. Davis, was trying to clean it out with this heavy-duty industrial spray, but I swear it just made it smell like lemon-scented tuna... 

Wait, what did you ask me? Blurting things out? Oh. Yeah, no, I don't really do that. I usually let people finish.
When you do start a task, how often do you find yourself stopping before you've finished it?

Stopping before I've finished? Um, yeah, that happens a lot, actually. Like, almost all the time. If my department chair gives me three or four things to do after a meeting, I usually start the first one, maybe even do most of it, but then the last step—like sending the file, updating the shared calendar, printing the handouts—it just doesn't happen unless someone reminds me. 

Our shared calendar system is this incredibly clunky software from like 2005. The interface is just awful, everything is this weird shade of beige, and the text is tiny. It reminds me of the computer we had in my middle school computer lab. We used to play Oregon Trail on those, the ones with the floppy disks. I always died of dysentery. It was practically a rite of passage. My friend Josh used to name all his party members after kids in our class, so it was always hilarious when someone got a snakebite. 

Josh actually became a snake breeder, which is wild. He lives out in Arizona now and has this whole temperature-controlled room just for his pythons. I went to visit him once, and it was so dry out there my lips were chapped the whole week. I had to buy this special medicated lip balm from a gas station, and it tasted like eucalyptus...

Wait, sorry. Stopping tasks, right? Yeah, I usually get most of the way there, but the very last step just kind of falls off my radar unless I get a reminder.
Do you ever find yourself becoming so absorbed in an activity that you lose track of time and forget about everything else around you?

Um, absorbed in something? Like losing track of time? No, I don't really think so. I mean, I don't really get sucked into things like that. I feel like I'm usually pretty aware of what time it is because we live by the bell at school. Every forty-five minutes, exactly. It's like Pavlov's dogs, you know? The bell rings, and you just automatically pack up your bag. 

I actually read this fascinating article about Pavlov and how he didn't originally set out to study classical conditioning. He was actually studying the digestive system of dogs. He won a Nobel Prize for it, which most people don't know. They just know about the bells and the salivating. My dog, Buster, he's a golden retriever mix, he starts drooling the second he hears the crinkle of a cheese wrapper. It doesn't even have to be his cheese. I could be opening a string cheese for myself, and suddenly there's a puddle on the hardwood floor. 

Hardwood floors are such a pain to keep clean, honestly. When I bought my house, I thought they would be so much easier than carpet, but every single piece of dust shows up. I bought one of those robot vacuums to help, but it just pushes the dog hair into these little tumbleweeds that roll around the hallway. The robot's name is Sir Sucks-a-Lot. My niece named it. She's five and she thinks it's a pet. She tried to feed it a carrot once, and it jammed the brush roller. I spent like two hours with a pair of tweezers trying to get it out...

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, losing track of time. Yeah, no, I don't really get hyper-focused like that. I'm usually pretty aware of the clock.
Do you have trouble keeping your workspace or living space organized?

Trouble keeping things organized? Um, well, I don't really know. I mean, my classroom is usually pretty decent because the janitorial staff comes in every night. But my desk... well, actually, my desk is kind of a mess. I have stacks of ungraded papers everywhere. 

I actually assigned this essay on the French Revolution last week, and I've only graded like three of them. The French Revolution is such a wild period to teach because the kids always get so hung up on the guillotine. They want to know all the gory details. I had to tell them we couldn't watch any videos about it because last year, a kid got lightheaded and actually passed out. Right there in the middle of second period. We had to call the nurse, Mrs. Higgins. 

Mrs. Higgins is great, but she always smells intensely of peppermint. She says it helps with nausea, which I guess makes sense for a school nurse. She gave me some peppermint tea once when I had a headache, but I accidentally left the mug on the roof of my car when I was driving home. I didn't realize until I hit the brakes at a stoplight and it just shattered all over my windshield. I had to pull into a car wash right then and there. Those automated car washes always make me feel claustrophobic, though. The big spinning brushes coming at the windows... it feels like you're inside a washing machine. 

Wait, what was the question? My workspace? Yeah, I guess my desk at school and my apartment are both pretty cluttered. I wouldn't say I'm super organized.
Do you find it hard to pay attention to details or make careless mistakes in your work or other activities?

Pay attention to details? Um, I don't really know if I'd say that. I mean, I don't think I make careless mistakes, really. I try to be pretty thorough when I'm putting together my lesson plans. 

Actually, I spent like three hours last Sunday just looking for the perfect font for this worksheet on the Industrial Revolution. I found this one that looks like old typewriter text, which I thought the kids would appreciate. Typewriters are having a huge moment right now, you know? My local coffee shop—the one on 4th Street with the really good cold brew—they actually have a vintage typewriter just sitting on a table for people to use. Someone typed out a whole poem about a squirrel on it last week. I read it while I was waiting for my drink. 

Their cold brew is amazing, but they use those paper straws that just disintegrate in your mouth after five minutes. I hate that texture, it's like chewing on cardboard. I actually bought a pack of metal straws to keep in my car, but they clink around in the cup holder and it drives me crazy. It sounds like someone is playing the triangle in the passenger seat every time I hit a pothole. And the roads around here are terrible right now because of all the construction on the highway. They've been working on that same overpass for like two years...

Wait, sorry. Careless mistakes? Yeah, no, I don't really think I have a big problem with that. I try to get things right.
Do you find it hard to stay focused on a task for as long as it requires to be completed?

Hard to stay focused? Yeah, actually, that's kind of the main reason I came in to see you. I can sit down at my desk with a stack of essays or a curriculum document, fully intending to get to work. But curriculum documents are honestly the worst right now. The district just rolled out this new software for logging our state standards, and they keep saying it's "streamlined," but it requires like seven clicks just to enter one single objective. 

The IT guy, Greg, did a whole presentation on it during our in-service day. Greg is a nice guy, but he wears these incredibly loud Hawaiian shirts. Like, neon flamingos and palm trees. I asked him where he gets them, and he said his sister sends them to him from Florida. Florida is so humid, I really don't know how people live there year-round. I went to Orlando once for a teaching conference and my hair just immediately puffed up like a dandelion. I had to go buy this special anti-frizz serum from a drugstore at midnight, and the cashier ended up talking to me for twenty minutes about her pet iguana that escaped into her air conditioning vents... 

Wait, sorry, what was I talking about? Oh, right, staying focused on a task. Yeah, so I'll sit down to grade or read those documents, and within ten minutes I realize I’ve just been staring at the exact same page the entire time. I'll be thinking about three other completely unrelated things, and I'm barely taking in a single word of what’s actually right in front of me.
Do you find it hard to control your emotions when you're feeling frustrated or annoyed?

Control my emotions? Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, I'm generally a pretty laid-back guy. Even when things get really annoying, I don't usually lose my temper. Like, the copy machine in the teacher's lounge is a perfect example. It jams literally every time I try to print a batch of quizzes, and it makes this horrible screeching noise like a dying bird. 

The only person who knows how to fix it is Linda, the front office secretary, but she's always on her lunch break right when I need her. She eats tuna salad every single day. The whole main office smells like it by noon. I actually used to love tuna until my dad took me on this deep-sea fishing trip off the coast of Maine when I was twelve. The water up there is absolutely freezing, even in the middle of August. You have to wear these thick, heavy rubber boots, and mine had a tiny hole in the toe, so my left foot was just soaking wet and completely numb for like six hours. We didn't even catch anything that day, just a bunch of seaweed and a rusty old crab trap. The boat ride back was so choppy I thought I was going to be sick over the railing...

Wait, sorry, what was the question again? Oh, getting frustrated. Right, yeah, no, I don't really have a hard time controlling my emotions. I just kind of roll with it when things go wrong.
Do you find that you can focus on a task for a short period, but then your attention starts to wander?

Focus for a short period and then it wanders? Yeah, I think I basically just said that, right? That's... that's exactly why I made this appointment. I sit down at my desk, you know, fully intending to get through a whole stack of essays or read through those new curriculum documents. I'll get everything set up, I'll have my red pen—well, actually I use purple now, because I read an article that said red ink is too aggressive and causes anxiety in students. 

Which makes sense, honestly. I remember getting papers back in middle school that looked like a crime scene. Mr. Henderson, my 8th grade history teacher, he used this really thick red marker. He was a terrifying guy. He used to make us memorize all the presidents in order, and if you messed up, you had to stand in the corner. I can still name them all up to Lincoln, but after that it gets fuzzy. Lincoln is fascinating, though. Did you know he's in the Wrestling Hall of Fame? Seriously, he only lost one match out of like three hundred. I tried to tell my students that last week to get them interested in the Civil War unit, but half of them were just watching TikToks under their desks...

Sorry, I'm doing it again. Um, but yeah, what I was saying before... I'll sit down to work, and like ten minutes later, I realize I haven't actually read a single thing. I'm just staring at the same page, and my brain is off thinking about three completely different things, and I haven't absorbed a single word. So, yeah, short periods of focus before my attention wanders... that's definitely me.
Do you often feel restless or have trouble staying seated when you're in a quiet environment?

Restless? Trouble staying seated? Um, no, not really. I don't feel like I have to get up and move around a lot. I'm fine sitting still. Even when it's super quiet, like during study hall. I actually kind of like the quiet sometimes. 

Though, to be honest, study hall is never actually quiet. There's always some kid tapping a pencil or whispering. Last week, I caught two of my sophomores trying to sneakily trade Pokémon cards under a desk. I didn't even know kids still collected those. I had a huge binder of them when I was ten. I had this holographic Charizard that I traded my neighbor for. His name was Kevin, and he was obsessed with skateboarding. He tried to build a half-pipe in his driveway once using scrap wood from a construction site down the street. It completely collapsed the first time he tried to drop in on it. He didn't break anything, but he scraped his elbow up pretty bad. His mom was a nurse, though, so she patched him right up. She used to make these incredible chocolate chip cookies... 

Oh, right, sorry. Staying seated. Yeah, no, I don't feel restless or have trouble staying in my chair. I can sit still just fine.
Do you think your difficulty in staying focused is affecting your daily life more than any other issue you're experiencing?

Yeah, honestly, I think it is. The focus thing is definitely the biggest problem right now. It's getting pretty bad at work. The missed follow-through on things has gotten serious enough that my department chair actually put me on a support plan. Which is incredibly embarrassing. 

She's this really intense woman, Dr. Aris. She wears these thick-rimmed glasses and always has this perfectly ironed silk scarf on. I don't know how she keeps them so pristine. I spill coffee on myself at least twice a week. Usually on Tuesdays, because that's when they have the good donuts in the lounge, the ones from that bakery down on 4th street. The maple bar there is unbelievable. My wife and I went there on our second date, actually. We walked all the way down to the waterfront afterwards. It was raining, but we didn't even care. We've been married for five years now. 

But, um, yeah, speaking of my wife... she's actually had to start taking over all the bills and the household reminders and stuff. She just can't count on me to keep track of them anymore. I kept forgetting to pay the water bill, and they almost shut it off last month. So she just handles it all now. It makes me feel terrible, like I'm not pulling my weight, you know? So yeah, the focus issue is definitely affecting my daily life the most.
Do you think your difficulty with staying focused is something that you've experienced for most of your life, or is it a relatively recent development?

Most of my life? Yeah, definitely. I mean, it's not new. Even back in primary school, my report cards always said the exact same things. It was like a broken record—"bright but careless," or "doesn't finish work unless closely supervised." My parents were constantly on my case because they'd find all these crumpled-up worksheets at the bottom of my backpack that I just completely forgot to turn in. 

Backpacks were so different back then, you know? I had this amazing Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles one in third grade. It was the kind with the hard plastic shell on the back so it looked like you actually had a turtle shell. I was obsessed with Donatello. He was the smart one who did all the machines. I tried to build a grappling hook out of a jump rope and a wire coat hanger once because of him. I threw it up into the big oak tree in our front yard and it got stuck on a branch. My dad had to get the extension ladder to get it down, and he was so mad because he was in the middle of watching a football game. The Bears were playing, and my dad is a huge Bears fan. He actually has a signed Mike Ditka jersey framed in his basement...

Wait, sorry. What was I saying? Oh, right, the worksheets in my backpack. Yeah, I'd do the homework, or at least start it, and then just... forget it existed. So, yeah, it's been like this for as long as I can remember, not just recently.
Do you think your difficulties with focus and completing tasks are related to your overall level of motivation or interest in the activities themselves?

Motivation? Um, I don't know. I mean, maybe? It's hard to say. Sometimes I'm really interested in what I'm doing, like when I'm putting together a new lesson plan on the Industrial Revolution. I love history. I actually went to this incredible museum exhibit last summer on early steam engines. They had this massive, fully restored locomotive right in the middle of the hall. It was painted this deep, glossy black with brass fittings that were polished so bright you could see your reflection in them. The docent there was this older guy, Henry, who used to work on the railways in the seventies. He had the most amazing stories about being snowed in on a freight run through the Rockies. Said they had to survive on canned beans and whatever they could find in the dining car for three days. My grandfather used to eat canned beans straight out of the tin. He always said it was a habit from his time in the Navy... 

But, uh, anyway. Motivation. I don't know if it's just about being interested. Even when I really want to do something, or I know it's super important—like getting my grading done so my students actually have feedback—I still just... hit a wall. So I'm not really sure if it's just a lack of interest, you know? It feels like something else.
Do you think your difficulties with focus and completing tasks are significantly impacting your relationships or daily functioning outside of work?

Yeah, it definitely is. I mean, I forget ordinary responsibilities way more than I want to admit. It's not just the big work stuff. It's the little things, like... like replying to a parent email, or paying a bill before the late notice comes in the mail. Or even just picking up something my wife asked for on the way home. She'll text me to grab milk, and I'll walk right past the dairy aisle because I'm thinking about... I don't know, what we're having for dinner. 

Speaking of dinner, we actually tried this new Thai place down the street last night. It's called Lemongrass, I think? Or maybe Basil and Lemongrass. Anyway, they have this incredible Pad Kee Mao. The noodles were perfectly chewy, and they put just the right amount of Thai basil in it. I love Thai basil. It has this slight anise flavor that regular sweet basil just doesn't have. I tried growing sweet basil on our kitchen windowsill once, but it died after like three weeks. I think I overwatered it. Or maybe underwatered it? I can never tell with houseplants. My mom has a green thumb, though. Her entire sunroom is basically a jungle. She has this massive Monstera plant that she's had since the nineties. It's so big it's practically taking over the room...

Wait, sorry. What was the question again? Oh, right, outside of work. Yeah, so, like I said, I just keep forgetting the basic day-to-day stuff, and it's definitely putting a strain on things at home with my wife. It's really frustrating.

Wait, sorry. What was the question again? Oh, right, outside of work. Yeah, so, like I said, I just keep forgetting the basic day-to-day stuff, and it's definitely putting a strain on things at home with my wife. It's really frustrating.
